definition: Interhemispheric transfer is the passing of information from one cerebral hemisphere to the other so both sides of the brain can contribute to processing. In this source, it refers specifically to transfer of auditory information between the hemispheres as part of listening performance.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence (“the passing of information from one cerebral hemisphere to the other”) is not explicitly stated or formally defined in the packet; the packet only mentions “transfer of auditory information between the two hemispheres” without giving this general definition.

The definition’s claim that the term refers specifically to transfer of auditory information “as part of listening performance” is supported only insofar as the study evaluates dichotic listening and other auditory tasks and concludes that advantages may be attributable to “transfer of auditory information between the two hemispheres,” but the packet does not provide a standalone meaning of the term limited to that context.
The packet supports a narrower, auditory-specific usage, but the first sentence gives a broader general definition of interhemispheric transfer that is not stated in the source.

The source describes transfer of auditory information between the two hemispheres as a proposed explanation for listening-performance findings; it does not define the term as a general brain-processing mechanism or say both sides contribute to processing in that way.
